# Two models of the spectrum {.divider}

**Goal.** IEC 61400-1 offers two densities for the longitudinal wind, Kaimal and von Karman.
Compare them, and carry the difference through to the noise and the design. The same
analysis is worked out under each: [Kaimal](q5-kaimal.html) &middot; [von Karman](q5-vonkarman.html).

## Two models: the formulas {.smaller}

Both are one-sided densities of $\varepsilon$ with the A.13 prefactor; Lao et al.
[\[LRKSG22\]](#references), eq. (18), use the second:

$$S^{\mathrm{K}}_\varepsilon(f) = \mathrm{TI}^2\;\frac{4L/\bar V}{\big(1+6fL/\bar V\big)^{5/3}},
\qquad
S^{\mathrm{vK}}_\varepsilon(f) = \mathrm{TI}^2\;\frac{4L/\bar V}{\big(1+70.8\,(fL/\bar V)^2\big)^{5/6}}$$

| | Kaimal [\[KWIC72\]](#references) | von Karman [\[vK48\]](#references) |
|---|---|---|
| value at $f = 0$ | $4L\,\mathrm{TI}^2/\bar V$ | $4L\,\mathrm{TI}^2/\bar V$ |
| above the corner | $\propto f^{-5/3}$ | $\propto f^{-5/3}$ |
| $\int_0^\infty S\,df$ | $\mathrm{TI}^2$ | $\mathrm{TI}^2$ ($70.8$ is $70.78$ rounded, the value that makes it exact) |
| IEC length, hub $\ge 60$ m | $L = 8.1\Lambda_1 = 340$ m | $L = 3.5\Lambda_1 = 147$ m (Lao et al.: $150$ m) |
| corner at $\bar V = 8$ m/s | $\bar V/6L = 0.0039$ Hz | $\bar V/(8.41L) = 0.0065$ Hz |

- **One family.** Both are the A.13 prefactor times a shape that is flat below a corner
  and falls as Kolmogorov's $f^{-5/3}$ above it. They differ in how the corner is turned.
- **Different $L$, on purpose.** IEC picks the two lengths so that the $f^{-5/3}$ ranges
  coincide: at $1$ Hz the densities agree to $0.2\%$. The price is the low end. The
  models disagree on the integral length scale itself ($340$ against $147$ m), and so on
  $S(0)$, by a factor of $2.31$.

## Two models: where the dither frequencies sit {.smaller}

![](assets/wind-spectra.svg){.fig-hero fig-alt="Kaimal and von Karman one-sided densities on log-log axes at 8 m/s and 10 percent turbulence intensity. Kaimal is 2.3 times higher at low frequency and turns its corner earlier; above about 0.02 Hz the two coincide along f to the minus five thirds. The dither frequencies of 600, 150 and 60 second periods are marked on both curves: at 600 s Kaimal is higher, at 150 and 60 s von Karman is. A dashed curve, the shaping filter of Lao et al., runs below von Karman at low frequency, above it near 0.08 Hz and below it again at high frequency."}

::: claim
The design reads each density at $f_1$ only. Kaimal over von Karman there: $1.35$ at
$T = 600$ s, $1.03$ at $314$ s, $0.81$ at $150$ s, $0.79$ at $60$ s. The published $150$ s
sits just above Kaimal's corner and on von Karman's.
:::

## Two models: what changes downstream {.smaller}

Links A to C never use the form of $S$. Link D and the closed loop read it at $f_1$, through
$S^{2s}(f_1)\,T/2$, so the choice enters as one ratio per period:

| $T$ | $S^{\mathrm{K}}(f_1)/S^{\mathrm{vK}}(f_1)$ | $\sigma(\tilde u)/u^\star$, Kaimal | $\sigma(\tilde u)/u^\star$, von Karman | measured ratio | $\sqrt{S^{\mathrm{K}}/S^{\mathrm{vK}}}$ |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| $60$ s | $0.794$ | $0.0257$ | $0.0288$ | $0.892$ | $0.891$ |
| $150$ s | $0.808$ | $0.0427$ | $0.0475$ | $0.899$ | $0.899$ |
| $600$ s | $1.353$ | $0.0693$ | $0.0596$ | $1.163$ | $1.163$ |

The loop of *Checked: the scatter of the loop*, run on both synthesized winds (same seeds, $24$
records of $20$ days per row). At the design level ($\tau_c = 1$ day):

| | Kaimal | von Karman |
|---|---|---|
| least loss at $T = 60$ s, $a_{\text{opt}}$ | $0.20\%$, $a = 9.1\%$ of $u^\star$ | $0.23\%$, $a = 9.6\%$ of $u^\star$ |
| published design ($150$ s, $13.6\%$) | $0.38\%$ | $0.40\%$ |

::: claim
Changing the model changes no derivation; it rescales the scatter at each $T$ by
$\sqrt{S(f_1)}$, exactly as *The noise a slow loop averages* says it must. Kaimal is the noisier
model at $T = 600$ s, von Karman by $11$ to $12\%$ at the short periods. The design rule and its
choice of $T = 60$ s survive the change of model; the loss it achieves moves by $0.02$ points.
:::

## Two models: the shaping filter of Lao et al. {.smaller}

Lao et al. do not synthesize from eq. (18). They pass unit white noise through a rational
filter and scale its output by $\sigma = I\,V_m$ [\[LRKSG22\]](#references), eqs. (19)&ndash;(21):

$$H_t(s) = \frac{K_F\,(m_1T_Fs+1)}{(T_Fs+1)(m_2T_Fs+1)},\qquad
T_F = \frac{L}{V_m},\quad K_F = \sqrt{\frac{2\pi T_F}{B(\tfrac12,\tfrac13)}},\quad m_1 = 0.4,\ m_2 = 0.25$$

- **Why a filter.** The exponents $5/6$ and $5/3$ are not integers, so no finite-order
  linear system has exactly the von Karman density; a filter is needed to generate the
  wind online, sample by sample. A.12 builds the whole record at once and evaluates $S$
  exactly on its frequency grid, so it needs no filter.
- **The variance is right.** For white noise of two-sided density $1$ the output variance
  is $0.98\,\sigma^2$: $K_F$ is the normalization.
- **The shape is approximate.** Their filter's density against eq. (18), at their
  $L = 150$ m, $V_m = 12$ m/s ($T_F = 12.5$ s):

| $f$ | $0$ | $1/600$ Hz | $1/150$ Hz | $1/60$ Hz | $0.08$ Hz ($fT_F = 1$) | $1$ Hz |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| $S_{H_t}/S^{\mathrm{vK}}$ | $0.75$ | $0.75$ | $0.84$ | $1.02$ | $1.37$ (largest) | $0.73$ |

Above the corner the filter falls as $f^{-2}$, not $f^{-5/3}$, so the ratio keeps falling as
$f^{-1/3}$.

::: claim
For ten-minute constraint tests, which is what Lao et al. need, the variance is what matters
and the filter gets it right. For this analysis, whose noise is $S(f_1)$, the filter's
error at the dither frequency ($0.75$ to $1.02$) is as large as the gap between Kaimal and
von Karman themselves, which is why A.12 synthesizes from the spectrum directly.
:::
